gen-fs-styro-gf-sofia-sans-semi-condense: Crowded, retro and loud: Styro packs its letters nearly shoulder to shoulder. And Sofia Sans Semi Condensed lets tall lowercase and generous entry curves do the quiet work, while the heading keeps all the swagger.
gen-fs-styro-gf-stack-sans-notch: Styro presses its letters tight, with barely any gap in the e or c. Stack Sans Notch is the opposite, its curves open to the eye and its strokes uniform like rod stock, so the heading shouts while the sans just talks.
gen-fs-styro-gf-stack-sans-text: Commanding and a bit retro, Styro hunches its letters together with almost no gap left in the curves. But Stack Sans Text draws a marker-like line with its curve endings kept well apart, so the heading does the pounding and the body does the explaining.
gen-fs-styro-gf-sulphur-point: Retro and commanding, Styro crams its letters until the e and c nearly seal shut. And Sulphur Point, with openings you can see into and a bulky, marker-like line, would carry a long read without any of that tension.
gen-fs-styro-gf-tiktok-sans: Letters pressed almost into each other give Styro its crowded, retro punch. TikTok Sans, with its spacious c, would read easily for pages.
gen-fs-styro-gf-ubuntu-sans: Styro is retro and crowded, its letters leaning together with hardly a gap in the e or c, while Ubuntu Sans sits below with big, bent-pipe curves. Styro earns its keep big and short.
gen-fs-styro-gf-vend-sans: Vend Sans reads like a ruler-drawn line with its wide, open curve endings. Against Styro's crowded, retro heading, that quiet precision is the strongest thing the pair has going.
gen-fs-styro-gf-yaldevi: Tight, loud and retro up top. Styro's crowded letters meet Yaldevi's plain sans, whose e opens clearly to the right, and that gap between shut and open is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-fs-tanker-gf-cascadia-code: Tanker's curves turn inward and its letters nearly touch, giving it a heavy, commanding mass. Cascadia Code answers with wire-thin, monoline strokes and wide spacing between neighbors, so the plain sans gives the page room to breathe under the weighty heading.
gen-fs-tanker-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono stands its letters like pins in a wide board. Tanker's heavy heading closes its curves and crowds its gaps, while the sans below keeps every bend open, so the page moves from dense to spacious.
